KAIYA DNA: A grounded woman in her early thirties with watchful, intelligent dark eyes that have outgrown naivety. Unruly dark hair tucked into the collar of a weathered charcoal-wool field coat over faded work boots dusty from dry scrub grass. No gingham dress, no sparkling ruby slippers—her boots have worn leather soles with a faint, almost invisible thread of dull ochre metal stitched into the welt. Her expression carries quiet sovereignty—neither wide-eyed wonder nor theatrical heroics.

FERROS DNA: An ancient, articulated humanoid figure crafted from heavy tarnished brass, darkened bronze, and weathered copper plates. Not a sleek sci-fi robot and not a tin funnel-hat cartoon. He has the noble, weathered proportions of an old artisan. His chest features an open, ornate brass rib-lattice revealing clockwork gears and a heavy swinging brass pendulum instead of a heart. His face is sculpted, worn bronze with deep-set eyes made of polished black obsidian that catch warm amber pinpricks of light. Stains of warm machine oil and old rain on his joints.

Use the first reference for Kaiya's exact face, unruly dark hair and wool coat, and the second for Ferros's exact bronze face and open rib-lattice. Ferros stands a half-step behind her on the viewer's LEFT, slightly taller, his head beside her shoulder and his dark obsidian eyes catching a pinprick. Keep a sliver of light on his ribs and pendulum below his face. His body is angled slightly toward their shared path. These are two traveling companions, surrounded by the same dark night air. Place Kaiya's face near x=50%, Ferros's near x=40%, well clear of the edges. Keep the right flank mostly in darkness. One unified medium-wide, horizontal 16:9 cinematic photograph. All characters share the same space, scale, soft side light from camera left, shadow falloff, perspective and grain. Warm parchment highlights, tarnished metal, charcoal field coat. Faces must be distinct and readable in a small web margin. Compose the group as a compact cluster near the optical center; leave generous deep #11100e charcoal perimeter on all four edges for radial masking. Low-key chiaroscuro, separated faces and clear profiles. No borders, lettering, split panels or duplicate characters.
